question: If the interest earned during the 2ⁿd year on a certain sum is ₹5,214, and the rate of interest is 10% per annum compounded annually, then the sum is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the principal be 100 units.

Interest for the 1st year = 10% of 100 = 10 units.

Interest for the 2ⁿd year = 10 units + (10% of 10 units) = 11 units.

Given, 11 units = ₹5,214

⇒ 100 units = (5214 ÷ 11) × 100 = ₹47,400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹47,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate (R) = 10% per annum compounded annually

Compound Interest for the 2ⁿd year = ₹5,214

**Formula Used:**

Amount after n years (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

CI for the nth year = Amount after n years − Amount after (n−1) years

 
 
 
 

 

 

 

 Principal (P)
 Amount 1
 Amount 2
 

 

 1st Yr CI = 10%
 

 

 2nd Yr CI = 11%
 
 ₹ 5,214
 
• 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount after 1 year = P(1 + 10/100)¹ = 1.1P

⇒ Amount after 2 years = P(1 + 10/100)² = 1.21P

⇒ Compound Interest for the 2ⁿd year = 1.21P − 1.1P

⇒ 0.11P = 5214

⇒ P = 5214 ÷ 0.11

⇒ P = 47,400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹47,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For 2 years at R%, the effective compound interest rate can be directly found using the successive percentage formula: R + R + (R × R)/100.

Compound Interest for a Specific Year

The compound interest for exactly the nth year can be directly calculated by evaluating: CIₙ = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ−¹ × (R/100).

Simple vs Compound Interest Difference

For the 1st year, both SI and CI are equal. From the 2ⁿd year onwards, CI becomes progressively greater because interest is recursively charged on the accumulated interest.
